Flow arcs between two points

Source: R/layers-arc.R
geom_arc_3d.Rd

Draws a parabolic arc from (x, y, z) to (xend, yend, zend), the flow-map arcs of deck.gl's ArcLayer. Arcs rise above their chord by height times the chord's horizontal length as drawn in the box (with the aspect of coord_3d()), so long flows arch higher than short ones and the shape does not depend on the x/y units. Arcs that rise above the box are clipped with the data unless coord_3d(clip_data = FALSE). Without z, arcs start and end on the floor of the box, over a map drawn with geom_sf_3d(). height can also be mapped.

Usage

geom_arc_3d(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  stat = "identity",
  position = "identity",
  ...,
  height = 0.25,
  n = 32L,
  arrow = NULL,
  na.rm = FALSE,
  show.legend = NA,
  inherit.aes = TRUE
)

Arguments

mapping, data, stat, position, ..., na.rm, show.legend, inherit.aes

Standard layer arguments.

height

Peak rise as a fraction of the horizontal chord length. Setting it overrides a mapped height.

n

Number of straight pieces per arc.

arrow

Arrow specification from grid::arrow().

Value

A ggplot2 layer.

Examples

flows <- data.frame(x = 0, y = 0, xend = c(4, -3, 1), yend = c(1, 2, -4),
  volume = c(3, 1, 2))
ggplot2::ggplot(flows, ggplot2::aes(x, y, xend = xend, yend = yend)) +
  geom_arc_3d(ggplot2::aes(colour = volume, linewidth = volume)) +
  coord_3d()
